San Miguel Ixtapan: Ceremonial centre in the Tierra Caliente of the State of México, in the municipality of Tejupilco, in a part of the country that has barely been surveyed.
Teotitlán del Valle: Zapotec town in the Tlacolula valley, 31 km from Oaxaca at the foot of the Sierra Juárez, known in Zapotec as Xaguixe, the place at the foot of the mountain, and known to everyone else for the wool rugs woven here on hand looms.
Valle de Bravo Petroglyphs: Carvings in the bed of the Presa Miguel Alemán in the State of México, a reservoir that drowned the valley in 1947.
Paracas Candelabra: A branching geoglyph cut into the northern face of the Paracas Peninsula, visible from boats crossing Pisco Bay.
Nuraghe Losa: A Bronze Age basalt nuraghe on the Abbasanta plateau.
Nuraghe Arrubiu: A large Bronze Age nuragic complex near Orroli, with a central tower enclosed by a five-tower bastion and additional outer defences.
Sacred Well of Santa Cristina: A descending stairway of carefully dressed basalt leads to a circular water chamber beneath a corbelled roof.
Sacred Spring of Su Tempiesu: A Nuragic water sanctuary built against a spring-bearing rock face near Orune.
Sanctuary of Santa Vittoria (Serri): A large Nuragic sanctuary on the plateau of Serri, with a sacred well, gathering spaces and the remains of other buildings.
Monte d'Accoddi: A raised prehistoric altar-platform approached by a long ramp near Sassari.
Monte Baranta: A Copper Age complex above Olmedo with a massive stone enclosure, a long wall and a horseshoe-shaped structure overlooking the cliff.
Nuraghe Orolo: A multi-tower nuraghe near Bortigali, with a tall central tower and a surrounding bastion.
Pranu Muttedu: A prehistoric funerary landscape near Goni, with standing stones, tombs and circular settings among cork oaks.
Tamuli Archaeological Complex: A Nuragic complex near Macomer containing a nuraghe, settlement remains and giants’ tombs.
Sa Coveccada Dolmen: A monumental slab-built dolmen near Mores, with an enormous capstone and an opening in its front slab.
Giants' Grave of Li Lolghi: A long collective burial monument near Arzachena, with a curved forecourt of upright slabs and a tall central stele.
Giants' Grave of Coddu Vecchiu: A giants’ tomb near Arzachena with a prominent arched stele, curved forecourt and a slab-roofed burial corridor.
Cucuruzzu (Corsica): A Bronze Age casteddu near Levie, where dry-stone walls and chambers incorporate enormous natural granite boulders.
Araghju (Corsica): A Bronze Age hilltop enclosure above the Porto-Vecchio plain.
Tappa (Corsica): A Bronze Age fortified settlement near Porto-Vecchio, with a stone tower and enclosure fitted to a rocky outcrop.
Ceccia (Corsica): A prehistoric tower site on a granite height near the village of Ceccia.
Funtanaccia Dolmen (Corsica): A collective burial chamber on the Cauria plateau, built from upright granite slabs supporting a single great capstone.
I Stantari (Corsica): Standing-stone alignments on the Cauria plateau, including human-shaped statue-menhirs with carved weapons and other details.
Renaghju (Corsica): A prehistoric standing-stone site on the Cauria plateau, with numerous granite menhirs in a landscape occupied over several periods.
Palaggiu (Corsica): A major concentration of standing stones in southern Corsica near Sartène.
Porta Saracena (Segni): A monumental gateway in the polygonal stone walls of ancient Segni.
Orto della Regina: Polygonal stone enclosure on Monte La Frascara in the Roccamonfina volcanic landscape.
Giants’ Tomb of Uore: Bronze Age collective tomb near Borore, with a semicircular facade and a partly buried arched stele.
Porta Aurea (Castellonorato): Monumental stone gateway and wall remains at Palombara near Castellonorato, Formia.
Ponte Alto (Terracina): Ancient road bridge on the Appian route northwest of Terracina.
Spacco della Regina (Ansedonia): Coastal rock cleft beside the ancient waterworks of Portus Cosanus, near Ansedonia.
Polygonal Walls of Amelia: Large fitted limestone blocks form the surviving southern fortifications of ancient Ameria.
Grotte di Torri: Polygonal masonry enclosure beneath a later rural building in Fara in Sabina.
Acropolis of Ferentino: Ancient acropolis beneath the cathedral of Ferentino, with polygonal masonry and Roman monumental building phases.
Acropolis of Circeii: Polygonal limestone fortifications on Monte Circeo above San Felice Circeo.
Polygonal Walls of Castel San Pietro Rom: Large dry-laid limestone blocks form the ancient fortification circuit above Palestrina.
Pyrgi Walls (Santa Severa): Polygonal walls of the Roman maritime colony, partly incorporated into the later Castle of Santa Severa.
Kazarma Bridge (Arkadiko): Bronze Age stone bridge on the ancient route between Tiryns and Epidauros.
Fonte di Uore: Spring structure near Borore, listed as Fonte Nuragica Uore in the Sardinian regional heritage inventory.
Caslasc (Giornico): Triangular dry-stone fortification above Giornico, also called Castellaccio.
Porta Foca (Segni): Ancient gateway in Segni’s polygonal stone fortifications.
Porta Sanguinaria (Ferentino): Southern gateway of Ferentino, with polygonal lower masonry, a Roman stone arch and later medieval work above.
Sanctuary of Pietrabbondante: Samnite sanctuary at Calcatello, with a monumental theatre and temples.
Trebula Balliensis: Archaeological area near Treglia, with large-block fortifications, a monumental gateway and Roman remains.
Santa María de la Piscina: A rock-cut cemetery lies beside the Romanesque hermitage near Peciña in La Rioja.
San Vítor de Barxacova Necropolis: Anthropomorphic graves cut into rock surround the remains of a medieval chapel above the Mao river in Parada de Sil.
San Andrés Necropolis (Sonsierra): About seventy rock-cut graves survive among the vineyards of San Vicente de la Sonsierra.
Regumiel de la Sierra Necropolis: An extensive early medieval cemetery occupies the sandstone outcrop around the church of San Adrián Mártir.
Cuyacabras Necropolis: Rock-cut graves and the remains of a church mark a deserted medieval settlement in the forest near Quintanar de la Sierra.
Castro de Ulaca: Granite walls enclose a large Iron Age hilltop settlement above the Amblés valley.
Quinta da Regaleira Initiation Well: Modern revival architecture, late 19th to early 20th century (estate construction programme: 1893–1920).
São João de Areias Churchyard Necropolis: Rock-cut graves survive at the parish church of São João de Areias.
Longroiva Castle: A granite keep and surviving enclosure preserve the medieval castle of Longroiva in Mêda.
Fontainhas Rock-cut Tombs (Folhadal): Two anthropomorphic graves are cut side by side into the same granite outcrop near Folhadal.
Largo do Colóquio Rock-cut Tomb: A single anthropomorphic grave lies on exposed granite at Folhadal’s western edge.
Orca do Folhadal: Granite slabs form the surviving chamber of this Neolithic funerary monument near Folhadal.
Orca de Pramelas: A polygonal granite chamber and short passage survive at this dolmen near Canas de Senhorim.
Orca do Pinhal dos Amiais: Nine granite uprights form the polygonal chamber of this passage grave near São João do Monte, in Senhorim.
Anta da Arquinha da Moura: A substantial earthen mound encloses a granite chamber and passage at this Neolithic tomb in Lageosa do Dão.
Anta da Cunha Baixa: A large capstone covers the granite chamber of this passage grave near Cunha Baixa in Mangualde.
Orca dos Padrões: Granite uprights define a chamber and passage on elevated ground near Cunha Baixa.
Oriu di Cubia: A doorway closes a naturally hollowed granite boulder on Monacia’s heritage trail.
Oriu di Grussettu: A vast granite overhang shelters a stone-walled enclosure above Monacia-d’Aullène.
Oriu di i Canni: A pointed granite shelter with a fitted stone façade, door and window.
